newsitem.title: CANADA: AMC Entertainment eying some Eaton stores.
newsitem.headline: AMC Entertainment eying some Eaton stores.

text.p: U.S. cinema firm AMC Entertainment Inc said on Friday it was considering some weak performing outlets of Canadian retailer T. Eaton Co Ltd, currently under creditor protection, as centers for mega- theaters.
"It just depends on the situation," said Harry Peckham, director of corporate business development for AMC'S AMC Theaters of Canada unit.

Many of the malls with Eaton sites lacked the right mix of leisure stores and cafes or restaurants, Peckham said. But he said it would consider sites where landlords considered a shift from fashion-based tenants.
AMC Theaters, whose parent is based in Kansas City, has already had a 30-screen movie mega-theater approved by Toronto city council.
Eaton's has said it may close up to 31 of its 85 stores. Seven are set to shut by June 30.
"We're looking at everything and trying to find the best opportunity in each market," Peckham said. AMC Theaters plans an entertainment complex in every major Canadian city.
Analyst Richard Talbot with Thomas Consultant said: "AMC is looking at 30 odd screens. so it will be fairly major."
U.S. retailer Sears, Roebuck and Co, has also said it wanted to expand in Canada, where it has a 55 percent stake in Sears Canada Inc.
Sears Chief Executive Arthur Martinez said on Thursday after the company's annual meeting that Sears was "actively looking for ways to expand" the its department stores in Canada.

"The bankruptcy of Eaton's puts a number of stores, if you will, into play," said Martinez. "We're not sure what the reorganization plan will produce, but we're watching and monitoring the situation."
Eaton, Canada's fifth largest department store, filed for creditor protection on February 27 and was expected to deliver a restructuring plan by June 15.
